extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of English literature and literary criticism (especially those studying Henry James and theories of the novel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative principles derived from Henry James's essay 'The Art of Fiction' for producing realist/modernist fiction that emphasizes impression, selection, and execution over didacticism or rule-bound composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel as a personal impression of life
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel, in its broadest definition, is 'a personal impression of life'; its value is greater or less according to the intensity of that impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer conveying filtered, individual impressions rather than exhaustive reportage of events; intensity of impression determines artistic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the work 'interesting' (the primary condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The only condition that I can think of attaching to the composition of the novel is … that it be interesting.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary objective is to engage and interest the reader; being instructive or amusing are valid aims insofar as they contribute to interest. Young novelists must learn to be worthy of the liberty to create interesting work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author's liberty: freedom to feel and say
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist must have 'freedom to feel and say' — artistic liberty to choose subjects, tone, and manner without being bound by prescriptive laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject rigid rule-books or imposed 'laws of fiction'; allow authorial freedom in subject selection and expression as central to artistic creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art of execution belongs to the author
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The execution belongs to the author alone; it is what is most personal to him, and we measure him by that.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate craft, style, and workmanship: how the author shapes material (tone, sentence-level work, structure) is a primary measure of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art is essentially selection — choose the typical and inclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Art is essentially selection, but it is a selection whose main care is to be typical, to be inclusive.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select incidents and details that are representative and illuminating rather than exhaustive; aim for selections that reveal broader patterns of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce an 'air of reality' — the illusion of life
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'air of reality (solidity of specification)' is 'the supreme virtue of a novel' — the illusion of life that makes other merits effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize concrete, specific details and textures that create the convincing look of things; other virtues depend on success in creating this illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to infer the unseen from the seen
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist should have 'the power to guess the unseen from the seen, to trace the implication of things, to judge the whole piece by the pattern.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train attention to implication and pattern: suggest interior life, social realities, and unseen forces through selected surface details and incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat experience as impressionistic (experience as a spider-web)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is 'an immense sensibility, a kind of huge spider-web… catching every air-borne particle'; impressions are the novelist's raw material, not complete reportage of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent experience via impressions and 'tints' rather than attempting total documentation; prioritize evocative traces over exhaustive facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize incidents and presentation over 'story' as soul
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The soul of a novel is not the story but incidents… Story is an idea that needs a form called the novel; the presentation of the story is the soul of the artistry.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on which incidents are chosen and how they are presented (tone, point of view, detail) rather than treating plot as the central artistic aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolve rigid distinction between character and incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions of character and incident are interdependent: 'What is character but the determination of incident? What is incident but the illustration of character?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate character depiction and incident selection so that each illuminates the other; avoid treating character and plot as wholly separate priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject didactic 'conscious moral purpose' as the primary aim
rubrics_metrics.description: James denies a required 'conscious moral purpose' for fiction; the author's role is not to preach but to present interesting impressions of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overt moralizing or preaching; moral resonance may emerge from the depth and quality of the author's mind and presentation, not from explicit didactic intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No precise laws or teachable recipe for artistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposes Besant's claim that fiction is governed by precise laws teachable like harmony or perspective; creativity 'cannot be taught' in that law-like way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on formulaic 'rules' as substitutes for sensibility and practice; encourage experiment and individual development rather than rule memorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art lives on experiment, variety, and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Art 'lives upon developing arguments, experiment, curiosity, upon variety of attempt, upon the exchange of views and the comparison of standpoints.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage experimentation, diverse approaches, and critical exchange; variety of attempts fertilizes fiction and expands possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistry is acquired by innumerable attempts, not divine gift
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistry is 'the result of innumerable attempts' rather than a natural gift or inspired miracle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value sustained practice, revision, and craft-building; persistence and repeated experimentation produce artistry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance/adventure can be an 'interesting' novelistic element
rubrics_metrics.description: James accepts romance (adventure, wonder, strangeness) as a legitimate source of interest in fiction; 'romance' need not undermine artistic worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss works with adventure or romantic elements out of hand; evaluate how such elements contribute to the work's interest and impression of life.
